To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the social support students receive from the formal support program, as well as overall perceived social support from friends and family, is related to students' identification with the nursing profession and their interest in nursing.

the university sponsored program positively influenced Native American nursing students' identification with the nursing major, their interest in the major, their perception of value of the major and their motivation to pursue nursing as a career, while perceptions of unfairness within the nursing major negatively affected the students' perception of value of and motivation to pursue a career in nursing.

overall perceived social and programmatic support positively influenced Native American nursing students' identification with the nursing major and their motivation to pursue nursing as a career, and perceived unfairness due to racism within the nursing major negatively influenced students' perception of nursing and their motivation to remain in the nursing program.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of social support on Native American nursing student success and motivation.
understanding the social factors that influence motivation to pursue a career in nursing among Native American nursing students.
the effects of perceived social support and racial bias on Native American students' motivation to pursue nursing as a career.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social support from the university-sponsored program positively affected the motivation of Native Americans in nursing.
the students' perceptions of social support, both from the program and from other sources, positively influenced their motivation to continue nursing.
the more social support students perceived, the more likely they were to be motivated to stay in the nursing program and to pursue a nursing degree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
formal support structures, such as a university sponsored support program, are important to students' success in nursing.
social support is a critical factor in the retention of Native American students within nursing.
the students' perceptions of the university-sponsored program and their perceptions of unfairness within the nursing program influenced their motivation to pursue nursing as a career.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the university sponsored support program positively influenced students' motivation to pursue nursing as a career, while perceptions of racial bias negatively influenced their motivation to pursue nursing.
social support can have a positive impact on Native American students' motivation and success in nursing.
social support from formal and informal sources is a critical component of Native American students' motivation to pursue a career in nursing.
